issue: Sentence-initial lower case »de« is a typography/grammar break; the translator used it to mark Koroviev's deferential third-person plural («Они»), but a lower-case sentence start reads as an error, and »De« would mean 'you'. «Herskabet» renders the honorific plural and echoes 12:15 «herskabets assistent» for «ихний помощник».

«Очень, очень приятно» as a greeting: «fornøjeligt» means 'amusing/enjoyable' and is odd as a pleased-to-meet-you formula. The README sample fix fixed «Очень приятно» as «Det glæder mig», which 15:98 also uses.
Addition: «lige på og hårdt» adds 'hard' (it is also a set phrase meaning 'bluntly'). The Russian has only «сразу».
russian: начать сразу с чего-то очень сильного
old: begynde lige på og hårdt med noget meget stærkt
new: begynde direkte med noget meget stærkt

issue: «прохрипела» means croaked/wheezed, not hissed. The same slip occurs at 10:133 («прохрипел» → «hvæsede»). 14:2 («прошипел») is correct.
Register: «наплевать» ('couldn't care less', literally 'spit on it') is colloquial but not vulgar; «sked på det» is cruder than the Russian.
old: i det hele taget sked på det
new: i det hele taget gav pokker i det

issue: Sense: «попросил свет оставить» means he asked for the light to be left on (it was already on). «få lyset tændt» says he asked for it to be switched on.
old: bad om at få lyset tændt
new: bad om at lade lyset være tændt

issue: Glossary break: GLOSSARY.md fixes гривенник = «tikopekmønt». «tiøren» is a Danish coin.
Sense inverted: «А что натворит, это уж будьте благонадежны» means 'and as for him making mischief, you can count on it'. «så kan De være helt rolig» reads as 'don't worry (he won't)'.
russian: А что натворит, это уж будьте благонадежны
old: Og hvad det angår, at han laver noget, så kan De være helt rolig.
new: Og at han nok skal lave noget, det kan De være helt sikker på.

issue: Danish grammar: «nederlaget … var ligesom at tage en del af min sjæl ud» is not grammatical (the subject is not the one doing the taking). The Russian has «как бы вынула у меня часть души».
russian: чудовищная неудача с этим романом как бы вынула у меня часть души
old: var ligesom at tage en del af min sjæl ud
new: tog ligesom en del af min sjæl ud af mig

issue: Consistency: тир is «skydebane(n)» in 10:2 and 10:126 (the same garden). «skydeteltet» adds a tent.
russian: из того низкого здания за тиром

issue: «промычал» means mumbled or lowed (inarticulate and low), not roared. The roar comes later, at 15:18 («рев»).
Gloss added: «из-под Эйнема» is just 'an (empty) Einem box'. «chokoladefabrikken» explains the brand, which the brief forbids.
«развившиеся волосы» means hair that has come loose or uncurled; «udredne» (combed out) is wrong and breaks the echo of 13:178 («развившуюся прядь» = «en løs hårlok»).
Register (Yershalaim chapters): the vocative «О» is «O» in the glossary motifs («O guder, guder»). The colloquial «Åh» undercuts Levi's solemn lament.
Addition: «провалялся на ней» means 'lay on it (sick)'. «vred sig» (writhed) is not in the Russian.
russian: провалялся на ней до рассвета пятницы
old: lå og vred sig på det

issue: Register: an invocation of God in the solemn chapters. «Åh, Gud» is a casual exclamation. Use the vocative «O», as in the glossary motifs.
Spelling: the indefinite singular is «bøddel». «bødl» appears only in the inflected forms (bødlen, bødler).
Sense: «хоть убей» here means 'for the life of me / kill me if you like (there's not one left)'. «ikke for alverden» means 'not for anything in the world' (a refusal).
russian: и теперь ни одной нет, хоть убей!
new: om man så slog én ihjel!

issue: Spelling: «billetkassereskeren» is missing an r (kassererske → kassererskeren).
Unidiomatic calque: «i den midaldrende alder» is not Danish. The Russian «средних лет небритый человек» is plain.
old: en ubarberet mand i den midaldrende alder

issue: Spelling/consistency: Danish uses «hr.» (as in 9:26, 12:17, 12:26, 33:13). «Herr» is German.
Spelling/consistency: «hr.», as at 18:87.
Sense: «Верьте ему!» means 'Believe him!'. «Tro på ham» means 'believe in him' (faith).
